title: Teaching bop-struck students who wanted to play like Dizzy
summary: Students arrived with a Dizzy Gillespie book unwilling to learn scales; he told them to learn the horn first and lost most pupils to Latin trumpeters.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Now when you had your studio and you were teaching, this is now in the what -- the mid '40's?
Now this is when bebop was really flowering?
And you were teaching young people?
They were interested in jazz, I assume?
Yes, oh that's what they were interested in. They came to me, because you know a lot -- I was being recommended.
And they would come to me -- they'd get their mother, father, somebody go down and buy them a horn and get them a Dizzy Gillespie book and they'd come up to my

studio and say I want to study, I want to learn to play trumpet and they'd show me this book. This kid said, look I want to play like Dizzy. I said I can't teach you to play like Dizzy Gillespie. The first thing you got to do is learn to play your horn, you got to learn to play the horn first. You got to learn everything about it. No, I don't want to learn -- they say I don't want to go through the scales and all that I want you to teach me to play like Dizzy. I say I can't. I don't think Dizzy could teach you to play like that.

I say, Dizzy's a fine trumpet player. And he's a schooled trumpet player. Before he started playing what he's playing now. So you've got to go through all that and it's going to take years. And some of them I'd never see again. I'd run into that all the time. How long will it take me to learn to play the trumpet. I'd say, you may never learn to play trumpet. Only thing you can do is start or try, go through -- like the things that we all had to do, start from the bottom. Then you see what happens. I lost most of my pupils over latin trumpet players.
